title: Hierarchical Assembly of Coordination Macromolecules with Atypical Geometries: Gd44Co28 Crown and Gd95Co60 Cage

material_class.structural_family: molecular crown assembled from four heart-like Gd10Co7 units

synthesis.procedure: The Supporting Information specifies the same aqueous-solution/MeCN preparation as for Gd95Co60, except that Co(OAc)2 is increased from 1.0 to 1.5 mmol. The mixture is stirred, heated at 80 °C for 2 h, filtered, and left to evaporate at room temperature. Pink square crystals form after 2 days.

reagents.name: iminodiacetic acid
reagents.amount: 0.5 M in 1 mL mixed aqueous H2IDA/NaOH solution

reagents.name: sodium hydroxide
reagents.amount: 0.5 M in 1 mL mixed aqueous H2IDA/NaOH solution, plus 1 M aqueous solution (1.8 mL)

reagents.name: cobalt(II) acetate
reagents.amount: 1.5 mmol, increased from the 1.0 mmol used for Gd95Co60

synthesis.temperature: 80 °C for reaction; room temperature for evaporation
synthesis.time: 2 h heating; crystals obtained after 2 days
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Stirred solution synthesis; filtered mixture transferred to a 25 mL flask for evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filter the reaction mixture and evaporate solvent at room temperature to obtain pink square crystals.

properties.summary: Magnetic susceptibility decreases on cooling, consistent with antiferromagnetic interactions and zero-field splitting. The cluster shows a substantial low-temperature magnetocaloric effect.

source_locations.location: Supplied catalog row RAVPOX; CCDC order corroborated by Supporting Information §1.3
Supporting Information §1.4.2, embedded after the main article in the supplied Markdown; shared procedure in §1.4.1

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Four Gd10Co7 heart-like units connect side by side to form a discrete crown-shaped Gd44Co28 core.

material_class.structural_family: molecular cage assembled from heart-like units and two crown-like units

synthesis.procedure: Mixed aqueous H2IDA/NaOH, Co(OAc)2, Gd(ClO4)3, NaOH, and Na2CO3 solutions are added to MeCN with stirring. After heating at 80 °C for 2 h, the mixture is filtered and transferred to a 25 mL flask for solvent evaporation at room temperature, yielding pink leaf-shaped crystals.
